plate_findings.evidence: Caption identifies a tibial shaft lesion; the in-text description reports an expansile lytic cortical lesion.
In-text description reports varying osteosclerosis around the cortical lesions.
Caption states that CT shows the extent of the tumor in the cortex; the in-text description reports cortical destruction.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Radiograph of a tibial shaft lesion explicitly presented as representative classic adamantinoma, with cortical osteolysis and reactive sclerosis described in the article. [raw subtype: classic] B: Lateral radiograph of a tibial shaft lesion explicitly presented as representative classic adamantinoma, with cortical osteolysis and reactive sclerosis described in the article. [raw subtype: classic] C: Axial CT demonstrates the cortical extent of a lesion in a case explicitly identified as classic adamantinoma; cortical destruction is directly described. [raw subtype: classic] D: Axial MRI shows the extent of the lesion and is presented in the classic adamantinoma figure. The in-text mentions high T2 signal tumor foci, but no specific allowed vocabulary key matches this MRI finding. in_text_mentions: OFD-like and classic AD showed similar imaging characteristics (Figs. 1 and 2). The tumor was located in the cortex of the tibia or fibula, which showed expansile lytic lesions with varying degrees of osteolysis and osteosclerosis. CT showed cortical destruction, with cysts separated by sclerotic bony septa. MRI revealed different tumor foci with high signal intensities on T2-weighted images and T1-weighted contrast-enhanced images. Imaging showed whether the lesions were fibro-osseous, but neither CT nor MRI was able to differentiate between OFD-like and classic AD. Fig. 1Representative image
